nodes.label: Ingredient data class (rawQuantity, quantity: Double?, unit, name, note)
nodes.norm_label: ingredient data class (rawquantity, quantity: double?, unit, name, note)
nodes.rationale: rawQuantity stores what the user typed so it round-trips exactly; nullable quantity distinguishes unparseable from zero (fixes B9).

nodes.label: KitchenFormatter (measurement display)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the cup/Tbsp/tsp 'measures you actually scoop' breakdown but snaps to measurable amounts: half-tsp precision with quarter/eighth below 1 tsp, cup fractions, fewest-parts-then-fewest-scoops selection. Replaces whole-number rounding, fixing bugs B1-B7.

nodes.label: KitchenUnit enum
nodes.rationale: Replaces the stringly-typed ALL_UNITS Pair<String,String> catalogue with a typed enum carrying family (VOLUME/WEIGHT/COUNT), system (US/METRIC), and toBase conversion factors.

nodes.label: QuantityParser
nodes.rationale: Returns Double? so parse failure is distinguishable from zero (B9); handles thousands separators (B8), ranges via low end + RANGE_LOW_END flag, Unicode fractions, and rejects NaN/Infinity/exponents/negatives.

nodes.label: Recipe data class (title, yieldAmount, yieldLabel, ingredients)
nodes.norm_label: recipe data class (title, yieldamount, yieldlabel, ingredients)

nodes.label: B1-B10 accuracy bugs (whole-number rounding in formatQuantity/formatOther)
nodes.norm_label: b1-b10 accuracy bugs (whole-number rounding in formatquantity/formatother)
nodes.rationale: The legacy engine rounds to whole numbers, doubling leaveners (B1), printing 'pinch' for quarter tsp (B2), and mis-scaling pt/qt/gal/fl-oz/weights; several bugs are locked in by tests that must be rewritten to the new spec.

nodes.label: Editor autosave (500ms debounce straight to Room)
nodes.norm_label: editor autosave (500ms debounce straight to room)
nodes.rationale: No Save button and no draft table; an app-scoped coroutine survives leaving the screen. A new recipe isn't inserted until it has a title or ingredient; a session-created recipe emptied before exit is deleted.

nodes.label: Quick scale scratch recipe
nodes.rationale: A normal autosaved recipe pre-titled 'Quick scale' with the first qty field focused; only inserted once the user edits something, so backing out saves nothing.

nodes.label: Room persistence (RecipeEntity/IngredientEntity, exportSchema, migrations)
nodes.rationale: Relational storage gives stable IDs, ordering, search, and rename-without-delete/insert; replaces the old single Base64/tab-delimited preference blob where name was the key.

nodes.label: Undoable delete via RecipeRepository.restore
nodes.rationale: Delete is undoable instead of confirmed: restore brings the recipe back with its original id and timestamps so it lands in the same list position; the editor saves pending edits first so Undo restores the latest version.

nodes.rationale: Biggest accessibility and data-entry problem in the app: name truncates at ~150-170dp, the three-across layout breaks at 200% font scale, and placeholder-only labels vanish once text is entered.

nodes.label: Multiplier chips (half/1x/2x/3x) + stepper on Scale View
nodes.norm_label: multiplier chips (half/1x/2x/3x) + stepper on scale view
nodes.rationale: Doubling/halving is the dominant use case; bare target-serving numbers read as multipliers with no unit, and typing on a decimal keypad is slower than a stepper.

nodes.label: Remove 'Edit ingredients' mode; swipe-to-delete + persistent drag handle
nodes.norm_label: remove 'edit ingredients' mode; swipe-to-delete + persistent drag handle
nodes.rationale: A mode toggle on a screen that is already editable is confusing; 'edit' really means reorder/remove. Swipe-to-delete with Undo matches the list pattern and frees a top-bar slot.

nodes.rationale: The main job is not the shortest path: a cook wants open recipe -> see scaled amounts -> cook, and routing 90% of opens through an edit form adds a needless step. Recommended: List tap -> Scale View with an Edit pencil action.

nodes.label: :core:domain module (pure Kotlin/JVM)
nodes.rationale: Must never depend on Android (no android.*, androidx.*, or Android Gradle plugins) so business logic stays portable and unit tests run fast on the JVM; purity is verified via a runtimeClasspath dependency check.

nodes.label: Pure-JVM :core:domain module (no Android imports)
nodes.rationale: A plain JVM module means the compiler enforces 'no Android in business logic', gives fast tests, and provides the cleanest source for the iOS/Swift port whose spec is the Kotlin test suite.
